summary: This benchmark investigates the causal mechanism of attribute declaration edits in Qwen2.5-14B using activation patching and structured attention masks across blocks 11-48. The experimental setup demonstrates that downstream answer reversals rely almost entirely on a direct attention edge from the final readout token to the edited declaration, with relay-only paths producing zero reversals across 512 test pairs. The methodology is precisely specified and statistically rigorous, though evaluation is limited to a synthetic Python attribute completion template on a single checkpoint.
strengths: Rigorous experimental design isolating direct vs. indirect attention paths with clear Boolean masking controls across 38 transformer layers.
Exact reproducibility details provided, including model revision hash, layer indices, ridge regression penalty, generator seed ranges, and execution command.
Appropriate statistical reporting featuring paired sample margins and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals across 512 balanced evaluation pairs.
Clean ablation baselines verifying that all three attention mask variants preserve accuracy on unedited programs.
weaknesses: Evaluated exclusively on a synthetic Python two-class single-letter attribute completion format, leaving open how well these findings generalize to real-world code or multi-token spans.
No official repository metadata attachment was provided alongside the submission, requiring a 'text_only' badge despite embedded links in the manuscript text.
Does not resolve which specific attention heads or sub-layers within blocks 11-48 mediate the direct read.
suggestions: Expand the benchmark to natural Python programs and multi-token identifier renames to test circuit stability outside synthetic templates.
Perform layer-wise and head-wise path patching between block 10 and block 48 to locate the specific attention heads responsible for the direct readout edge.
Formally register the code repository in the submission metadata to qualify for an open verification badge.

claims.text: The only checkpoint is the frozen Qwen2.5-14B base revision 97e1e76335b7017d8f67c08a19d103c0504298c9.
Cross original and edited source state with three Boolean causal masks for blocks 11–48.
The Studio run lasted six minutes and 52 seconds using Python 3.12, MLX 0.32.4, MLX-LM 0.32.2 and NumPy 2.5.5.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Localizing Model Behavior with Path Patching
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies path patching and attention edge isolation to modern 14B parameter causal models (Qwen2.5-14B) specifically on in-context code declaration routing rather than toy syntactic English tasks on GPT-2 small.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
